newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil firms on good buying.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil firms on good buying.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed late on Wednesday on aggressive buying, brokers said.
They said a Chinese national oil company was in the market to buy the gas oil swap on the back of demand for the Chinese New Year in February next year.
December gas oil was last traded at $32.03 a barrel and quoted at $31.95/$32.15, up 25 cents from this morning's and Tuesday's quotes of $31.70/$31.90.
January gas oil was last traded at $31.30 and quoted at $31.25/$31.40, up from $31.00/$31.15.

The bullish sentiment on the jet fuel market on talks of an expected rise in regional demand during the Moslem fasting month in January supported the regrade, or jet fuel/gas oil spread. It was quoted at $1.80/$2.10 a barrel and traded earlier on Wednesday at $1.95.
The December regrade was relatively lower with quotes at $1.45/1.60.
Both the heavy and light ends remained untraded and were steady since Tuesday.
December fuel oil was quoted at $120.75/$121.75, and January at $119.00/$1119.75 a tonne.
December naphtha was quoted at $23.40/$23.65 a barrel and January at $23.40/$23.70.
